October 6, 2026

Trump says Iran could "take out" Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing calls of treason

tags: politics, war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

At a rally in Nebraska, President Donald Trump said of Iran, "let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego," describing the prospect as "a very small price to pay" for keeping the country safe, in remarks that also referenced high gasoline prices. Rep. Derek Tran called the statement treasonous and questioned the president's mental fitness, while San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said the city is "not collateral damage" and asked to be left out of "your reckless war talk." California Governor Gavin Newsom directed the State Threat Assessment Center to monitor whether foreign actors interpret the remarks as an invitation to target California. San Diego is home to a large Navy and Marine Corps presence.

Russian plague lab researcher's death prompts quarantine of nearly 200 contacts

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @groundnews

A 28-year-old researcher at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute died after developing pneumonia of "unknown" origin, with reports that a test tube broke in her hands; nearly 200 contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities denied a laboratory accident exposed her to plague, with Rospotrebnadzor saying no dangerous pathogens tied to her work were found, though Buryatia leader Alexei Tsydenov earlier said she died "possibly from the plague." The World Health Organization said the public health risk appears low and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the situation was not cause for alarm but warranted monitoring. Trump said he was concerned, that the United States was "looking at it very strongly" and stood ready to help Russia, while referring to it as a pneumonia plague and describing microbes as having grown stronger, "like an army."

Whistleblower who exposed Lutnick-Epstein business ties dies in Thailand

tags: legal, politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

Simon Andriesz, a former BGC Partners executive who raised concerns with regulators about business ties between Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Jeffrey Epstein, reportedly died by suicide in Thailand on September 23 at age 57. Andriesz found 2018 emails showing Lutnick and Epstein discussing Adfin, a digital advertising startup both Epstein and Cantor Fitzgerald had invested in, casting doubt on Lutnick's account of limited contact with Epstein. He also alleged embezzlement of broker bonus money at BGC and uncovered a 2013 proposal in which Lutnick sought to offer former Prince Andrew a £1 million loan; BGC denied misconduct. After he reported alleged retaliation, the UK Financial Conduct Authority found insufficient evidence, and following his death MPs called for an independent review and the FCA appointed board member Lea Paterson to examine its handling of the case.

Yemeni government launches offensive to retake territory from Iran-backed Houthis

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched a campaign to seize all areas held by the Houthis, with President Rashad al-Alimi saying forces would fight "until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia" and the military urging Houthi fighters to surrender. The Houthis seized the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and about 150 kilometres of Red Sea coastline last month and have advanced near Taiz, threatening the city's last road to Aden. The Houthis said they struck Saudi Aramco sites with missiles and drones after 50 Saudi-led attacks in Yemen, which Saudi Arabia has not confirmed. The United States is providing intelligence support to Riyadh.

Whistleblower says Trump ordered FBI investigations into protesters he saw on TikTok

tags: surveillance, immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A whistleblower complaint sent to the Senate Judiciary Committee alleges that on at least one occasion in 2025, Trump reviewed a TikTok video of anti-ICE protesters and demanded the FBI open an investigation into them. CNN reported the matter concerns the Los Angeles area, and the complaint says the FBI opened preliminary investigations of protesters who were allegedly using bullhorns to warn neighbours about immigration enforcement operations. Democratic senators are seeking to determine how many additional investigations have been opened into people the president saw on social media.

Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez and Merkley introduce bill to ban federal use of Flock cameras

tags: surveillance, politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Jeff Merkley introduced the Ban Flock Act, which would bar federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers or accessing data collected by them, and block federal grants from funding state and local contracts for the technology. More than 120,000 cameras from Flock Safety, one of the largest providers, were installed last year. Sanders said the company is "eviscerating the very notion of privacy" and warned against America becoming a surveillance state. The proposal follows reports of officers misusing license plate databases, including to stalk former partners, and Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced a separate bill last month targeting local purchases of the technology.

US and Mexico deploy troops to border after Coast Guard unit fired upon

tags: immigration, defence, politics
sources: @groundnews

About 500 US troops were deployed to Texas' Rio Grande Valley on Saturday after gunfire was directed at a Coast Guard unit near the US-Mexico border, with no personnel injured. Mexico deployed 159 naval personnel, 11 vehicles and two drones to its Tamaulipas border under Operation Sable, which its government described as part of coordinated "mirror operations" with the United States. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott said cartel involvement was "what I've heard" and a Border Patrol union official said it could be confirmed as a cartel, while Mexico says it has found no evidence the shots came from its territory.

New York declares state of emergency over measles outbreak

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency as measles cases grow, with up to 108 cases confirmed this year, including 92 since July. Pennsylvania is experiencing its own outbreak with more than 1,000 cases confirmed this year, compared with 17 cases in 2019. The United States is on pace for its worst measles year in decades.

Former MAHA figures object to coal-powered AI data center buildout

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

The administration is considering the use of coal-fired power to supply a large expansion of AI data centers, drawing objections from public health advocates. Multiple former members of the Make America Healthy Again movement associated with Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s campaign have written to the administration saying the plan contradicts campaign promises on health and the environment. Critics argue the scale of the buildout and its fossil fuel demand would harm air quality and surrounding communities.

Public comment closes on plan to strip protections from 45 million acres of national forest

tags: climate, politics, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

The Trump administration is seeking to erase protections covering 45 million acres of national forest, including about 4 million acres in Utah, with the public comment period closing October 6. Advocates note the agency is required to respond to issues raised in public comments, and that comments become part of the administrative record judges would review if the rule change is challenged in court.

Campaign warns Senate races could determine whether Mike Lee reaches the Supreme Court

tags: politics, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

Justice Samuel Alito, 76, told CBS he would consider retiring again next year, after a new Senate takes over in January. Sen. Mike Lee of Utah clerked for Alito twice, has appeared on every Trump Supreme Court shortlist since 2016, and the chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee has said he would recommend Lee for Alito's seat. Advocates are urging voters in states with Senate races this November, including Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas, to vote against the nomination path, citing Lee's post following the killing of Minnesota lawmaker Melissa Hortman and her husband and his effort to force the sale of up to 3.2 million acres of public lands.

Former House Speaker Dennis Hastert dies at 84

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Dennis Hastert, the Republican who served as speaker of the US House from 1999 to 2007, died Saturday at 84 while in hospice care at his home in Plano, Illinois, according to the Kendall County Coroner's Office. He pleaded guilty in 2015 to violating banking laws while withdrawing money used to conceal his sexual abuse of teenage boys; prosecutors said he molested at least four boys, some as young as 14, while working as a teacher and wrestling coach, but statutes of limitations prevented abuse charges. He was sentenced to 15 months in prison and served 13. In Congress he lent his name to the unwritten Hastert Rule, limiting floor votes to bills backed by most of the majority party.

Supreme Court hears case over where veterans can challenge VA benefits laws

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Supreme Court heard argument in the case of Army veteran Floyd Johnson, who has an 80% service-connected PTSD rating but is paid at the 10% rate because he is incarcerated for felony convictions. The justices are considering where veterans may challenge the constitutionality of federal VA-benefits laws.

Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump has approved execution by US Army firing squad for former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 at Fort Hood in 2009 and sentenced to death in 2013. If carried out, it would be the first US military execution since 1961 and the first Army firing-squad execution since 1945. No execution date has been set.

Arizona appeals court tosses sentence over AI-generated victim impact video

tags: legal, tech
sources: @groundnews

The Arizona Court of Appeals ordered Gabriel Paul Horcasitas resentenced for the 2021 shooting death of Christopher Pelkey, finding an AI-generated victim impact video used at his May 2025 sentencing was unreliable because it portrayed invented statements as Pelkey's own. The panel wrote that the video "presents a depiction of the victim and his thoughts created from the imaginings of the victim's sister." Pelkey's family used recordings, photos and videos to recreate him in what is believed to be a US court first, with the AI version saying "in another life, we probably could have been friends." Horcasitas, 55, was convicted of manslaughter and endangerment after fatally shooting the unarmed Pelkey, 37, during a Chandler road rage encounter; his lawyer argued the judge violated due process by relying on material he could not rebut.

Diesel prices force school districts to cut bus routes

tags: economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

School districts across the country are adjusting or cutting bus routes as diesel prices rise, according to Axios, requiring children to walk longer distances to bus stops. Cherry Creek Public Schools outside Denver is short about 40 drivers and is covering routes on an all-hands basis. The effects reported include students missing school-provided breakfast, arriving late to first period and losing access to school activities, with low-income children most affected.

Global survey finds growing view that social media harms democracy

tags: media, politics
sources: @groundnews

A Pew Research Center survey across 37 countries found views of social media's effect on democracy have grown more negative since 2022 or 2023, with negative assessments rising in 16 of 26 countries with comparable trend data and increases of about 20% in Germany, Hungary, Poland and Japan. Across all 37 countries, a median 55% still said social media has been good for democracy versus 35% who said it has been bad, while in the United States 64% called it bad, unchanged from 2022. A median 79% said social media makes people easier to manipulate with false information and 68% said it increases political division, while 77% said it makes people more informed and 60% said it gives people a more meaningful voice in politics.

Palm Beach County Republican Party endorses clerk candidate facing child abuse charges

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Palm Beach County Republican Party has endorsed Michael Caruso, the suspended incumbent running for Palm Beach County Clerk and Comptroller, despite pending charges. Caruso is accused of sexual abuse of a child under the age of five and is charged with kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child, and child abuse causing mental illness.

VFW opposes proposed VA rating changes for tinnitus and sleep apnea

tags: politics, defence, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Veterans of Foreign Wars renewed its push against proposed changes to VA disability ratings for tinnitus and sleep apnea. The organisation says the changes could reduce future disability compensation by $57 billion over 10 years and affect up to 1.5 million veterans. Current ratings are protected and the proposal is not law.

Pentagon's new cyber pay system could cut $1,000 a month for some troops

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Some Army cyber troops could lose up to $1,000 a month in incentive pay under the Pentagon's new compensation system. Internal guidance pointed affected soldiers toward Army Emergency Relief assistance.

Air Force graduates most pilots in at least 25 years under shortened training

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Air Force graduated 1,550 pilots in fiscal year 2026, its highest total in at least 25 years, while cutting military undergraduate pilot training to about nine months. Students now learn the basics at civilian flight schools before moving to military flying, simulators and virtual reality. At Laughlin Air Force Base, the washout rate fell from 5.7% to 4.0%.

Oklahoma Guardsman deployed to Washington arrested over personal pistol

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Spc. Jakob Noonan, 22, an Oklahoma National Guardsman deployed to Washington, D.C., was arrested after police found his personal 9mm pistol during a traffic stop. Noonan told officers the gun was registered to him in Oklahoma but acknowledged he did not hold a D.C. concealed-carry permit. He was off duty and out of uniform at the time.

Actor urges Jewish community to reconsider Netanyahu's conduct in Gaza

tags: politics, war
sources: @ericmoutsos

An actor recounted encountering Benjamin Netanyahu years ago when Netanyahu was Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, saying he instinctively moved his infant son away from him before learning who he was. He called on Jewish people worldwide to consider what Netanyahu and his right-wing government are doing, describing him as the most dangerous factor for Jewish people and saying the harm to children and civilians in Gaza is unconscionable and unsustainable.

Man convicted of shooting Marine veteran who was left paralyzed

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A jury convicted Wilmer Vladimir Ruiz Ortega of shooting Marine veteran Jimmy Friesenhahn, who was left paralyzed. Friesenhahn, who served four tours in Iraq, was working security when he discovered a handgun during a pat-down and a struggle followed. Ruiz Ortega now faces up to life in prison.

Cornell students and faculty demand leadership accountability over Jane Doe case

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Students at Cornell University have staged campus protests calling for the university president to resign, and thousands of alumni have signed on to efforts to hold the administration accountable, citing the handling of 2024 allegations from a plaintiff identified as Jane Doe. Faculty have introduced a no-confidence resolution stating the Faculty Senate has no confidence in the central administration's ability to address the ongoing crisis, and are pushing for systemic top-down change. The no-confidence vote is scheduled for next week.
